correctness.rationale: For arbitrary real symmetric X=[[m+d,z],[z,m-d]] with Frobenius PSD projection X_+, spectral eigenvalues m+-r, r=hypot(d,z), provide exact positive/mixed/negative formulas. In the mixed region the input-coordinate partial derivatives of output (11) and (12) have absolute row sums. With c=d/r, s=abs(z)/r, t=m/r these are optimized on t=-1,0,1 and c^2+s^2=1, yielding 3/2 for each diagonal and 9/8 for each off-diagonal, both strict away from rank-one limits. Piecewise segment integration yields global bounds; if a line is entirely determinant-zero, all its points share one rank-one direction and entrywise 1-Lipschitz holds. Explicit rank-one perturbations give first-order equality approach, so no two distinct finite matrices attain either larger Lipschitz supremum. Block embedding gives only L_n>=3/2, not sharp n>=3. Independent random finite-difference directional checks sampled 20,000 mixed-region perturbations; observed slopes below respective targets (1.4848,1.1148); the analytic inequality, not samples, proves uniform optimality.
